messages:
sarah: quick question — i'm seeing product put feature flags into the console while platform adds rollout policies to the API config. who is meant to own precedence when both exist? :thinking:
kevin: are you talking about per-route traffic splits vs ff gates? can you paste an example?
anika: yeah, e.g. we have two places to configure: the feature flag rule the product team creates and the `rollout_policy` in the service deployment. like:

```
// product feature flag (console)
feature_flag: {
  name: "new_rerank",
  rules: [{ audience: "beta_users", pct: 100 }]
}

// platform rollout (api/deployment)
rollout_policy: {
  type: "canary",
  traffic_split: 0.05,
  guard: { max_qps: 200 }
}
```

kevin: so if a request comes in and the platform canary says 5% but product.ff says beta_users -> 100%, which wins?
tj: short answer: we don't have a clear contract today, which is the problem. current behavior: runtime applies rollout_policy first (routing), then feature flags are evaluated on the device/user after routing. that's why some beta users get routed off the bucket.
anika: that's causing confused dashboards — product sees FF evals showing 100% for their cohort but our telemetry shows only ~5% hitting the new model.
sarah: that mismatch is exactly the ask. product expects flags to control exposure. platform expects rollout policies to protect capacity/latency. both are valid but we need documented precedence and UX in console.
tj: proposal: define an explicit layering order and a simple override rule. suggested precedence (from highest to lowest): 1) explicit per-request override (trace/debug), 2) deployment-level rollout_policy (platform guard + default split), 3) feature-flag routing (product intent), 4) global defaults. meaning platform can set a hard guard that prevents >X QPS or routes out of canary even if ff matches. product flags can request a higher exposure but cannot break platform guards.
kevin: +1 on guards being higher priority. maybe wording: "guards are safety, flags are intent". product needs visibility though — show in console when flag's intent was blocked by guard.
anika: telemetry change needed: when a request is rejected/redirected by rollout_policy we should emit an event `rollout.blocked_by_guard` with details (flag_id if present, route, reason). put that in per-flag timelines.
tj: API changes: we should add `evaluations` to the routing decision payload so downstream logs include: `decision_chain: ["rollout_policy:canary(5%)","feature_flag:new_rerank:true"]`. small schema: `decision_chain: [string]` (ordered).
sarah: UI/UX: in the console feature flag page show a compact "effective exposure" metric which is the intersection of flag intent and platform routing. tooltip explains layering.
kevin: implementation note: runtime already knows the routing bucket before ff eval; adding a single extra telemetry field is cheap. product side OK to show blocked counts?
anika: yes, product wants a graph: requested exposure vs actual exposure per hour. that will reduce confusion.
tj: ops question: who owns the canonical source-of-truth for rollout config? platform maintains deployment YAML (and runtime reads it). product manages ff rules in the console. we should add a reconciliation process that renders an "effective rollout" view and warns on conflicts at save-time.
sarah: agreed — UX action items: 1) add "effective exposure" to flag page, 2) show guard blocks, 3) surface conflict warnings when saving flags/deployments.
kevin: engineering action items: 1) add `decision_chain` to routing logs, 2) emit `rollout.blocked_by_guard` events, 3) add reconcile check in the console API.
anika: also add a small note in docs: "Guards (platform) are safety-first and can limit feature flag exposure. Feature flags express product intent but do not override platform safety limits."
tj: i'm happy to own the runtime telemetry + API bits. can someone from product own the console surface and docs?
sarah: anika, can you take the product side?
anika: yep. i'll draft mockups and doc language.
kevin: i'll take the reconciliation / save-time warnings (eng-platform).
deply-bot: deploy-bot: link to runbook: https://internal/runbooks/rollout-precedence (posted automatically) :rocket:
sarah: perfect — let's sync in the rollout sync on Tue. i'll add a short RFC. :thumbsup:
